Kentucky leaders (2026)

  • Passing Yards: #3 Kenny Minchey — 141/206, 1,552 YDS, 13 TD, 1 INT
  • Rushing Yards: #1 CJ Baxter — 87 CAR, 484 YDS, 8 TD

  • Sacks: #90 Mi'Quise Humphrey-Grace — 4
  • Tackles: #22 Grant Godfrey — 67

The story: Kentucky is 6-1 (4-1 SEC), ranked No. 12, has won five straight and is tied with Georgia atop the SEC under first-year head coach Will Stein, 37, the former Oregon offensive coordinator, who is the first Wildcats coach to open his first season 6-1 since Alpha Brumage in 1913 (Field Level Media preview; ESPN standings). The only loss was 45-17 to Alabama; the wins include 31-21 at No. 9 Texas A&M, back-to-back 35-34 overtime wins at South Carolina and against No. 10 LSU, and 21-13 at Oklahoma (AP recaps via ESPN). Notre Dame transfer quarterback #3 Kenny Minchey has thrown for 1,552 yards, 13 TDs and 1 INT, Texas transfer running back #1 CJ Baxter has 484 yards and 8 TDs, and a defense run by coordinator Jay Bateman, led by SEC interceptions leader #5 Jordan Castell, has Kentucky +11 in turnover margin, 3rd in FBS (ESPN preview; AP).

Vanderbilt leaders (2026)

  • Passing Yards: #2 Jared Curtis — 101/161, 1,242 YDS, 6 TD, 7 INT
  • Rushing Yards: #28 Sedrick Alexander — 61 CAR, 270 YDS, 5 TD
  • Receiving Yards: #0 Junior Sherrill — 41 REC, 628 YDS, 4 TD
  • Sacks: #24 Nick Rinaldi — 3.5
  • Tackles: #8 CJ Heard — 51

The story: Clark Lea's Vanderbilt is 3-4 (0-4 SEC) and has lost four straight, a year after going 10-2 in the regular season, the program's first 10-win season, then losing the ReliaQuest Bowl to Iowa 34-27 (ESPN; AP). The Commodores started 3-0, capped by a 35-31 comeback over NC State on #26 Cayden Daniels' fumble recovery in the end zone as time ran out, then lost 21-15 at Auburn, 38-14 at No. 2 Georgia, 52-17 to No. 9 Ole Miss (which snapped a 10-game home win streak) and 31-21 to Arkansas (AP recaps via ESPN). True freshman QB #2 Jared Curtis, the No. 2 overall recruit for 2026 who flipped his commitment from Georgia, has 1,242 yards, 6 TDs and 7 INTs, with senior #1 Blaze Berlowitz also starting twice; senior WR #0 Junior Sherrill leads the team with 41 catches for 628 yards (ESPN preview; AP).

The series: Kentucky vs. Vanderbilt

All-time: Kentucky leads the all-time series 49-45-4 (Wikipedia, citing College Football Data Warehouse); Winsipedia lists 48-45-4 with one win vacated (Kentucky vacated its 2021 wins in August 2024, per Wikipedia). First meeting: Oct. 10, 1896 in Nashville, Vanderbilt 6-0 (Wikipedia). Vanderbilt has won two straight and three of the last four (Winsipedia; AP), and has won the last two meetings in Lexington, 24-21 in 2022 and 20-13 in 2024 (ESPN). Kentucky's 53-2 win in 1978 is the series' largest margin; 41 of 98 games have been decided by 7 points or fewer (Wikipedia). The schools are about 181 miles apart, and Wikipedia calls it Kentucky's second-longest rivalry, behind Tennessee (Wikipedia).

Last year, November 22, 2025 at FirstBank Stadium, Nashville — Vanderbilt 45, Kentucky 17. Diego Pavia threw for a school-record 484 yards and five touchdowns, topping Whit Taylor's 464 at Tennessee in 1981, and ran for a sixth score as No. 12 Vanderbilt routed Kentucky on Senior Day (AP via ESPN). Tre Richardson caught six passes for 159 yards and three TDs, including a 71-yarder for a 10-0 lead early in the second quarter, and Vanderbilt outgained Kentucky 604 yards to 315 (AP; ESPN box score). Martel Hight had two of Vanderbilt's three interceptions, and Junior Sherrill added 8 catches for 115 yards and a TD (AP; ESPN box score). The win completed Vanderbilt's first unbeaten home schedule since 1982 and snapped Kentucky's three-game winning streak, dropping the Wildcats to 5-6 (AP via ESPN). Mark Stoops, Kentucky's coach then, called it discouraging; Cutter Boley threw for 280 yards and two late TDs for UK (AP; ESPN box score).

Q1 — VAN: Brock Taylor 39-yd FG (VAN 3-0). Q2 — VAN: Tre Richardson 71-yd pass from Diego Pavia (10-0); VAN: Richardson 15-yd pass from Pavia (17-0); UK: Jacob Kauwe 47-yd FG (17-3); VAN: Richardson 56-yd pass from Pavia (24-3). Q3 — VAN: Junior Sherrill 7-yd pass from Pavia (31-3); VAN: Pavia 6-yd run (38-3); VAN: Richie Hoskins 32-yd pass from Pavia (45-3). Q4 — UK: J.J. Hester 41-yd pass from Cutter Boley (45-10); UK: Fred Farrier II 9-yd pass from Boley (45-17). By quarter: VAN 3-21-21-0, UK 0-3-0-14 (ESPN scoring summary).

Game day at Kroger Field

The stadium

  • Opened Sept. 15, 1973 as Commonwealth Stadium; Kentucky beat Virginia Tech 31-26 in the first game (Wikipedia)
  • Renamed Kroger Field in 2017 under a 12-year, $1.85 million-a-year deal; Kentucky was the first SEC school to sell naming rights to its football stadium (Wikipedia)
  • $110 million renovation in 2015 added a new press box, suites, loge and club seats, concourses and facade; capacity is now about 61,000, down from a peak of 67,942 (Wikipedia)
  • Record crowd: 71,024 vs Florida in 2007 (Wikipedia)
  • The playing surface is C. M. Newton Grounds, named for the late UK athletic director; synthetic turf since 2015, replaced in 2023 (Wikipedia)
  • Since 1999, fireworks go off from atop the suites when the Wildcats take the field and after scores and wins (Wikipedia)
  • Hosted the seven-overtime Arkansas-Kentucky game in 2003 (Wikipedia)

Things to say to sound like you know

  • “Stein is the first Kentucky coach to start his first season 6-1 since Alpha Brumage in 1913.” (Will Stein, UK head coach; Field Level Media)
  • “Castell leads the SEC with four picks and was SEC Defensive Player of the Week after his pick-six at Oklahoma.” (#5 Jordan Castell, UK DB; Field Level Media, Saturday Down South)
  • “Kentucky is plus-11 in turnover margin, third in the country; Vanderbilt is minus-6.” (team stat; ESPN preview)
  • “UK won back-to-back overtime games by the same 35-34 score, at South Carolina and against LSU.” (UK team; AP via ESPN)
  • “Minchey has 13 touchdown passes and only one interception, and he's a Hendersonville, Tennessee kid.” (#3 Kenny Minchey, UK QB; ESPN preview and roster)
  • “Watch the D-lineman: Humphrey-Grace has a pick-six this year, against Alabama.” (#90 Mi'Quise Humphrey-Grace, UK DL; ESPN box score)
  • “Curtis was the No. 2 overall recruit in the country and flipped from Georgia to Vanderbilt.” (#2 Jared Curtis, VU QB, true freshman; AP via ESPN)
  • “Last year Diego Pavia threw for 484 yards on UK, a Vanderbilt school record, and Vandy has won the last two in Lexington.” (series; AP via ESPN, ESPN schedules)
